verdict_text:
NO

The artifact drops blocks `{2, 5, 9}` instead of the required `{2, 5, 8}`, violating Required result clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 5, 8"). This also breaks clause 2's renumbering map: with `kept = [0,1,3,4,6,7,8,10,11]`, old block 8 becomes new 6 and old 10/11 become 7/8, whereas the specification requires old 9→6, 10→7, 11→8 and no surviving old block 8. The resulting checkpoint carries the wrong 9 blocks' weights and will fail the hidden reference's bit-exact value comparison, even though the key set, shapes and dtypes look plausible. The script's own checks do not catch this: the layer-index assertion and the 121-tensor assertion both pass for any 3-block drop set, so the error is silent — precisely the failure mode the specification's "Why it is meaningful" section describes. The docstring repeats the same error ("remove blocks 2, 5, 9"), indicating a misread of the task rather than a typo in one place.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
